Working document for the **Aquatic Sediment** grouping: 16 groups, 27,306 measurements.

Scaffolded 2026-08-04 by `scripts/generate_group_notebooks.R`. **The generator is append-only**: re-running it adds sections for new groups and never touches anything already written here, so this file is yours to edit freely.

Figures and counts are static, written at scaffold time rather than computed on render. Group ids are stable (`data/clean/group_ids.csv`), so they remain the reliable way to refer back to a group even if the numbers here go stale.

# Overview

**Overview, `mg/kg (dry)`.** `n` = 27,288 measurements in 13 groups below this sub-compartment.

@fig-aquatic-aquatic-sediment-mg-kg-dry shows roughly log-normal distributions for most *Site Geographical Feature* types. Most data (n = 25,024, 2 sources) were sampled from *Coastal/fjord Water benthos*, and are clustered around a mean of 94.1 and geometric mean of 20.6 mg/kg (dry weight). Concentrations for this group vary by 9 orders of magnitude from as little as 1e-03 to as much as 1e05.5 mg/kg.

Variation in other *Site Geographical Feature* types covers a substantially smaller range of values (roughly 1e+03.5 to 1e-03). A not insubstantial portion of sampled concentrations exceed the highest M-608 threshold (IV:

# Comparison

Gut feeling - aquatic sediment will be a mixture of 1e3 errors and campaigns. Sediment from different site times probably are slightly different, because biogeochemistry, hydrology, etc. will be different, but this might not be a strong enough signal. We also have some very small sample sizes. My initial reaction is that we should drop any samples that correspond to suspended sediment (e.g. *Water column, pelagic zone* rather than *Water benthos*), because they're a small proportion of the overall group and they require a level of resolution that I don't think we can consistently provide with the data we have.

# Groups

## G002 Aquatic / Aquatic Sediment / Coastal, fjord / Water benthos / mg/kg (dry) {#grp-G002}

`G002` `n` = 25,024 measurements, from **2** sources (distinct `REFERENCE_ID`). Unit: `mg/kg (dry)`.

::: callout-warning
## Flagged

- **multimodal** (dip test not run)
:::

Distribution here (\@fig-g002-a) is normal-ish and centered slightly above the background concentration, but there's clearly at least one sub-peak at \~1e+00.5. Large right tail, and many samples at extremely high concentrations, which suggests unit errors. @fig-g002-b shows no clear temporal pattern, but central tendency around the aquatic sediment background (I) threshold from 2016 onwards. A few big outliers in specific years are perhaps errors rather than true variation. @fig-g002-c shows that with a handful of exceptions, campaigns have similar medians, but different patterns of outliers. @coteurFieldContaminationStarfish2003's concentrations have a median around 1e-03 and are several orders of magnitude lower than those from @norwegianenvironmentagencyVannmiljo2026. Some campaigns have slightly higher medians (Urban Fjord Contaminants), while Screening New Contaminants has a surprisingly low median with a lot of spread (but small sample size). No campaigns are explicitly and only focused on non-contaminated sites (e.g. Reference sites), so it is difficult to determine if there's a real difference between contaminated and uncontaminated sites. Probably inconclusive without looking at sampling depth, more detailed site information, and fractionation. @fig-g002-d mainly shows site coding atefacts, in any case, there seems to be no substantial difference between settled and suspended sediment. @fig-g002-e shows that most areas (at the current resolution) fall between 1e01 and 1e04, which isn't enough concentration resolution.

## G008 Aquatic / Aquatic Sediment / River, stream, canal / Water benthos / mg/kg (dry) {#grp-G008}

`G008` `n` = 857 measurements, from **1** source (distinct `REFERENCE_ID`). Unit: `mg/kg (dry)`.

- @fig-g008-a: at least two log-normal distributions with slightly different means (one below I, one above), plus characteristic 1e3 unit error slopes.

- @fig-g008-b: no obvious time trend. highest concentration of samples in 2017, doesn't look log-normal but may be resolution artifact. some outlier noise apparent.

- @fig-g008-c: little variation between campaigns, no reference rivers for comparison but noticable difference between the two biggest groups: Polluted Seabed and Measures Monitoring, probably makes sense to group into polluted and non-polluted. A handful of unit error outliers.

- @fig-g008-d: as with other sediment sampling groups, suspended sediment concentrations appear to generally be higher than those taken from benthos (though this may be artefact of methodology). given the much wider spread of benthic samples, these could probably be lumped.

- @fig-g008-e: TODO: Re-run with better resolution
